title: Use the CPU-only torch wheel index for the jobs that do need torch
summary: The default PyPI torch wheel bundles CUDA kernels that are dead weight on a GPU-less runner. Pointing at download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu cuts it from ~527 MB to ~200 MB for the quality jobs.
description:
Follow-on to CIW-4, which removes torch from three jobs entirely. This story addresses the jobs that legitimately need it — `benchmark`, `benchmark-nightly`, `benchmark-scale`, and `codspeed` — where `sentence-transformers` requires torch for real embedding models.

GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runners have no GPU. The default PyPI `torch` wheel ships bundled CUDA kernels and cuDNN that can never execute there.

Work:

- Add an `extra-index-url` input to `.github/actions/setup-bench-python/action.yml`, defaulting to empty so existing callers are unaffected.
- Db2-quality jobs pass `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu`.
- If CIW-7 lands first, express this through uv instead — `[tool.uv.sources]` with an explicit CPU index and `torch = { index = "pytorch-cpu" }` — which is more reproducible than an `--extra-index-url` flag and avoids the index-priority ambiguity that `--extra-index-url` has with pip.
- Confirm `sentence-transformers` still loads and produces identical embeddings on the CPU build — the quality-tier IR metrics (BM-17, AGQ-3, AGQ-4) must not shift. Run `benchmarks/quality/ -m benchmark_nightly` before and after and diff the scores.

Risk: if any quality benchmark silently depends on CUDA availability for a fallback path, this surfaces it. That is a finding worth having, not a regression.

Depends on CIW-4 landing first (the extras split determines which jobs this applies to).

Done when: quality jobs install the `+cpu` torch build and IR metric outputs are unchanged.

comments.author: implementation
comments.text: Implemented via uv sources (CIW-7 path, landed first). pyproject.toml: added [tool.uv.sources] with torch = { index = 'pytorch-cpu' } and [[tool.uv.index]] declaring https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu with explicit=true. uv only uses the CPU index for torch; all other packages resolve from PyPI. Cuts torch wheel from ~527MB to ~200MB on the jobs that need it (benchmark, benchmark-nightly, benchmark-scale, codspeed). setup-bench-python/action.yml: added inline comment. NOTE: uv.lock must be regenerated with `uv lock` after merging.
